# Calendar widgets cache markup while keeping instance setup separate

Five frequently used Calendar widgets move parsing into lazy static fragment getters. Each getter imports the parsed template and replaces the constructor's fragment getter with that value. connectedCallback keeps its delayed-connection/child guards and appends a deep clone. The month-item and timed-event subclasses provide their own templates. Localization registration, node lookups, editing/navigation listeners, gripbars and state remain on the instance path. Existing display/navigation tests check visible results; they do not directly test parse counts, cached-fragment identity or loading speed. Later accepted accessibility roles are a separate phase. Native parser/DOM internals and cross-document or locale-change behavior were not executed or independently paired.

Scope: Calendar custom-element markup lifecycle.
